feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it claims no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 4 (58.54, best, body 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.08 m, y=0.05 m, 16 mm, kp 1.35). Raising inertia hurt: body_length 0.24 gave 30.8 (iteration 10) and mass 1.0 gave 42.7 (iteration 6). Lowering inertia is the direction you are testing, but the only lower-inertia evidence (iteration 2, 47.8) also moved the sensors to y=0.07, so it does not isolate the effect. Your 0.15 m step is small, and I have kept the iteration 4 controller so the change is isolated. This is the final race on an unseen track, so the score will not feed another iteration. The changes below are conditional on the next race result, which you will not see for this design, so they are best read as the rule you would apply if another iteration were run.
requested_changes: If a later race shows body_length 0.15 m scoring at or above 58.5 with max_error or steering_oscillation falling: keep 0.15 m and test body_length 0.12 m next. Evidence: inertia rising hurt sharply (iteration 10, body 0.24 m, 30.8), so the direction of lower inertia is the one still open.

If the score falls below about 56, or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2: return body_length to 0.18 m, the iteration 4 value. Evidence: iteration 4 at 0.18 m is the best measured design, and both inertia directions have been tested only with other variables changed.

Keep wheel_track 0.08 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg and y=0.05 m unchanged. Evidence: iterations 5, 6, 7 and 8 each moved one of these and scored 41.4, 42.7, 57.9 and 41.1, all below iteration 4 (58.54).
